features.name: Conamara Chaos
features.description: Conamara Chaos is Europa's showcase example of disrupted ice. Blocks of older crust appear to have broken apart, rotated, drifted, and refrozen in a darker matrix, giving scientists a rare look at how warm ice or shallow liquid water can remodel the surface.

details.label: Approximate extent
details.value: About 800 by 400 km

details.label: Science value
details.value: A key analogue for possible exchange between Europa's surface and ocean-bearing interior

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Bright rafts embedded in darker, mottled terrain near low northern latitudes

features.name: Murias Chaos
features.description: Murias Chaos, nicknamed the Mitten, is an elevated chaos terrain on Europa's leading hemisphere. Unlike the classic broken-raft look of Conamara Chaos, Murias is often interpreted as the surface expression of a large warm-ice diapir that rose through the shell, breached the surface, and spread material outward.

details.label: Approximate size
details.value: About 116 by 77 km

details.label: Nickname
details.value: The Mitten, named for its distinctive outline

details.label: Science value
details.value: A rare example used to test whether some chaos terrain forms by diapiric uplift and cryovolcanic extrusion

features.name: Thera Macula
features.description: Thera Macula is a dark, irregular patch in Europa's southern hemisphere. It is commonly interpreted as young chaos terrain where warm material rose through the ice shell, thinning or breaking the surface and leaving behind a chemically distinct deposit.

details.label: Why it matters
details.value: Often discussed as a candidate place where ocean-derived material may have reached shallow depths

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Dark southern feature close to Thrace Macula and Cyclades Macula

features.name: Thrace Macula
features.description: Thrace Macula is one of the dark reddish spots that interrupt Europa's bright icy plains. Its colour and texture point to contaminated ice, salts, or hydrated materials concentrated where the crust has been disturbed.

details.label: Feature type
details.value: Macula: a dark spot or patch on an icy world

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Dark patch paired with nearby Thera Macula in the southern hemisphere

features.name: Cyclades Macula
features.description: Cyclades Macula is a named dark patch in Europa's high southern latitudes. It helps show that Europa's surface chemistry and thermal history vary strongly from place to place rather than forming a uniform ice shell.

details.label: Diameter
details.value: About 107 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: IAU Gazetteer center latitude and west longitude

features.name: Castalia Macula
features.description: Castalia Macula is a broad, dark, young-looking depression on Europa. Studies of this region connect its mottled texture to local resurfacing, collapse, and the movement of warm or briny material within the ice shell.

details.label: Nickname
details.value: Often described as one of Europa's dark spots

details.label: Science value
details.value: Useful for comparing collapse-style terrain with blocky chaos terrain

features.name: Agave Linea
features.description: Agave Linea is a long ridge-and-trough belt formed as Europa's brittle ice cracked under Jupiter-driven tidal stress. Dark material along the fracture likely includes salts or non-ice contaminants brought upward and altered by radiation.

details.label: Feature type
details.value: Linea: an elongated bright or dark marking, ridge, or fracture system

details.label: What it records
details.value: Repeated opening, shear, and refreezing in Europa's mobile ice shell

features.name: Argo Linea
features.description: Argo Linea is one of Europa's long, dark lineaments. Its scale and continuity make it a useful guide to the global stress fields that have fractured Europa's surface through time.

details.label: Visual cue
details.value: Long dark band crossing brighter icy plains

details.label: Earth analogue
details.value: Some Europan double ridges are compared with refrozen cracks and meltwater features in terrestrial ice sheets

features.name: Belus Linea
features.description: Belus Linea is a dark triple-band feature imaged by Galileo. Bands like this are among Europa's most distinctive landforms: paired margins and a central bright stripe suggest repeated cracking, widening, and infilling by material from below.

details.label: Formation clue
details.value: Diffuse dark margins may record erupted or intruded debris along the crack

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Dark banding near the anti-Jovian hemisphere

features.name: Cadmus Linea
features.description: Cadmus Linea is part of Europa's dense network of named ridges and bands. Its position among crossing lineae shows how Europa's surface preserves multiple generations of stress, extension, and resurfacing.

details.label: Reading the surface
details.value: Where lineae cross, the younger feature usually cuts across or disrupts the older one

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Low-latitude banding amid brighter icy plains

features.name: Rhadamanthys Linea
features.description: Rhadamanthys Linea is a prominent named fracture system on Europa. It belongs to the world-spanning pattern of ridges and bands that reveal an ice shell continually stressed by orbital resonance with Io and Ganymede.

details.label: Orbital link
details.value: Europa's 2:1 resonance with Io keeps its orbit slightly eccentric, sustaining tidal flexing

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Elongated ridge system west of the central anti-Jovian terrain

features.name: Tyre
features.description: Tyre is a large multi-ring impact structure and one of Europa's clearest examples of a major impact into an icy shell. Its concentric rings are interpreted as the crust's response to impact energy moving through ice over a warmer, weaker layer.

details.label: Diameter
details.value: About 140 km

details.label: Why craters are rare
details.value: Europa's young surface has been repeatedly resurfaced by tectonic and icy processes

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Bright circular ring structure in the northern hemisphere

features.name: Pwyll
features.description: Pwyll is Europa's freshest and most visually striking crater. Bright rays of excavated ice stretch far from the impact site, crossing older ridges and plains and making the crater easy to identify on global maps.

details.label: Diameter
details.value: About 26 km

details.label: Visual cue
details.value: Bright ray system radiating across darker lineated terrain

details.label: Science value
details.value: Fresh ejecta exposes cleaner ice from below Europa's radiation-darkened surface

features.name: Cilix
features.description: Cilix is a small, well-preserved impact crater near Europa's equator. It is especially important for mapping because the longitude of its center defines Europa's longitude system, anchoring the 0-360 degree west-longitude convention used by the global texture.

details.label: Diameter
details.value: About 15 km in the IAU Gazetteer; NASA topography products describe the impact structure as about 20 km across

details.label: Mapping role
details.value: Defines 182 degrees west longitude on Europa

details.label: Topography
details.value: Galileo stereo imaging shows raised rims, wall slumping, and a central massif on the crater floor

features.name: Manannan
features.description: Manannan is a young impact crater whose ejecta and disturbed surroundings provide a window into Europa's near-surface structure. Like Pwyll, it is valuable because fresh impacts excavate material before radiation can fully alter it.

details.label: Feature type
details.value: Simple impact crater with surrounding ejecta

details.label: Science value
details.value: Fresh impact material helps constrain the composition and strength of Europa's upper ice shell

features.name: Tara Regio
features.description: Tara Regio is a geologically complex region that includes reddish, disrupted terrain and lineaments. Spectral studies have linked parts of this area with salts or altered ocean-derived materials concentrated on the trailing hemisphere.

details.label: Feature type
details.value: Regio: a broad named region with distinct appearance

details.label: Science value
details.value: Candidate area for studying non-ice materials on Europa's surface

features.name: Powys Regio
features.description: Powys Regio marks a broad province of mottled and lineated terrain. Large regions like this help connect local landforms to Europa-wide resurfacing patterns and to the changing stress field of the rotating ice shell.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Broad southern terrain province cut by many lineae

details.label: Interpretation
details.value: A regional record of older plains being overprinted by younger fractures and bands

features.name: North Polar Region
features.description: Europa's north polar terrain receives intense bombardment from particles trapped in Jupiter's magnetosphere. Radiation changes surface ice chemistry, creating oxidants and reddish contaminants that may eventually be cycled downward.

details.label: Environment
details.value: Strong radiation processing from Jupiter's magnetosphere

details.label: Astrobiology link
details.value: Surface oxidants could become chemical energy sources if transported into the ocean

features.name: South Polar Region
features.description: Europa's south polar region is important because possible water-vapour plumes have been reported there in Hubble observations. If active plumes exist, they could offer a way to sample ocean-related material without landing.

details.label: Observation note
details.value: Plume detections remain challenging and have not been continuously confirmed

details.label: Mission value
details.value: A plume fly-through could sample material sourced from Europa's ice shell or ocean
